translation: This is what is produced by rich and beautiful food. Such a person must frequently eat sweet and beautiful things and be very fat. Fatness makes one internally hot; sweetness makes one full in the middle; therefore the qi overflows upward and, turning, becomes wasting-thirst (消渴). The Tong Ping Xu Shi Lun (通評虛實論) says: Wasting dan (消癉), sudden collapse (僕擊), hemiplegia (偏枯), wei and reversal (痿厥), and qi fullness with counterflow (氣滿發逆) are the diseases of rich and noble people—the illnesses of rich food (膏粱).
translator_notes: 通評虛實論 kept as chapter name; 消渴 rendered 'wasting-thirst'; 膏粱 rendered 'rich food'.
